messages:
alex-rm: Heads-up: NordBank POC (tenant=nordbank-poc-12) hitting SSO + SCIM snags. Azure AD assertion arrives but users can't access the Console (401). SCIM sync reports 403 when attempting to update group membership. Also hosted API key creation in-console blocked with 'auth_method claim missing'. Can someone pick this up?

sam-se: Thanks. Are they using the built-in Azure AD gallery app or a custom SAML app? Also paste a redacted assertion if possible.

alex-rm: They used the gallery app with a couple of custom attribute mappings. Redacted assertion shows:```
<NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient">_abc123</NameID>
<Attribute Name="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress">
  <AttributeValue>test.user@nordbank.com</AttributeValue>
</Attribute>
<Attribute Name="auth_method">
  <AttributeValue></AttributeValue>
</Attribute>
```
They claim `auth_method` is set in the app but it's not arriving.

priyanka-devex: NameID transient can be fine if we map `email` to the Email field, but `auth_method` being empty would block API key creation — our guard requires a value like `mfa` or `pwd+mfa` for hosted keys. For SCIM 403, do we have the scim_request_id?

alex-rm: scim_request_id=scm_b9ff, log snippet:```
{"status":403,"detail":"service principal lacks group_modify scope","tenant":"nordbank-poc-12","scim_request_id":"scm_b9ff"}```

nina-support: Azure tends to create a provisioning service principal with minimal scopes. If they used the gallery app, you must explicitly grant the app the `Group.ReadWrite.All` Graph permission and then consent. Did IT grant delegated permissions or app-only?

alex-rm: IT says they set up the gallery app and granted admin consent for provisioning, but their dev says they used a custom service principal for SCIM. Not sure of exact permission set.

jordan-sre: Checklist: (1) Confirm SAML attribute mapping for email OID vs simple `email`. (2) Check `auth_method` mapping in Azure app Single Sign-On -> Attributes & Claims. (3) For SCIM, ensure the Azure provisioning app's service principal has `Group.ReadWrite.All` and the OAuth token matches the SCIM token in tenant config. (4) Tenant policy `allow_scim_group_writes` might be off.

alex-rm: How can I check the tenant policy? customer can't access Console yet.

emma-ps: I can query control plane: tenant_id=nordbank-poc-12, org=org_3f4c. Policy `allow_scim_group_writes` is true for this tenant. So group writes should be allowed. That suggests the SCIM service token or Azure permission is the issue.

idp-bot: Observed 12 SAML assertions in last hour with empty `auth_method`. Source: azure-nordbank-sso-app. Correlation cid-77d2.

nina-support: If the SCIM call returns 403 with 'service principal lacks group_modify scope', it means Azure's provisioning identity is missing Graph permission. Ask them to capture the `Authorization` header from one of the SCIM calls (ok to redact token body) so we can check fingerprint against our stored token.

alex-rm: Asked IT to paste the provisioning logs and one SCIM request header. They returned a provisioning log showing `Provisioning service: appId=0a1b2c3d` and a screenshot that looks like Group permissions granted. But the SCIM request header they pasted shows `Authorization: Bearer <opaque>` and the token kid doesn't match our stored key.

sam-se: If the token kid doesn't match, the tenant likely configured a different SCIM token than they think. Two fixes: (A) reconfigure Azure to use the SCIM token we issued, or (B) we reissue a token and have them update the Azure provisioning app. Nina, can you help them rotate?

nina-support: I'll walk them through reissuing a SCIM secret from the Console and updating the Azure provisioning app. Also ask them to re-run full sync after.

alex-rm: IT updated the SCIM secret to the new one and triggered a full sync. SCIM now creates users but group update still fails for a subset of groups (finance-apps). Error for those groups: 409 conflict with detail "externalGroupId already linked to another group".

jordan-sre: 409 conflict indicates duplicate externalGroupId mapping - likely they previously provisioned a group under a different tenant or we have a stale mapping. We can unlink the stale mapping if it's safe. Ask for the externalGroupId in the SCIM request payload.

alex-rm: Provided payload snippet for failing request:```
{"schemas":[],"externalId":"ext-gp-9001","displayName":"finance-apps","members":[...]}
```
They say that externalId is reused across multiple apps in their Azure tenant.

priyanka-devex: We recommend unique externalIds per Redwood group to avoid collisions. Short term: we can clear the stale mapping for `ext-gp-9001` after confirming which group in their tenant to keep. I'll prepare instructions and a rollback note.

alex-rm: Meanwhile hosted API key creation still blocked. After SCIM fixes, users still see `auth_method` empty. IT insists Azure app is sending `auth_method` claim based on conditional access policy (MFA) but maybe it's in `http://schemas.microsoft.com/claims/authnmethodsreferences` instead of `auth_method`.

sam-se: We support either claim but have to map it in the app settings. Show them how to add a claim mapping:
```
Name: auth_method
Source: Attribute - user
Source attribute: http://schemas.microsoft.com/claims/authnmethodsreferences
Format: Basic
```

alex-rm: Sent mapping instructions. They updated and re-tested. New assertion shows `auth_method` present as `http://schemas.microsoft.com/claims/authnmethodsreferences: pwd+mfa`. Hosted key creation still failing with 422 `registration blocked: policy requires verified_auth_method`.

emma-ps: Our hosted key policy requires the auth_method to match an allowlist (`mfa`, `pwd+mfa`). The incoming value has the full URI prefix in attribute. We need them to map to one of the allowlist values or we can extend the matcher to accept the prefix for POC. Security prefers updating mapping.

priyanka-devex: For POC speed, offer two paths: (1) they trim the claim in Azure so it emits `pwd+mfa` (preferred), or (2) we temporarily accept the URI-prefixed value for the tenant for 48h. I'll ask security.

idp-bot: Security exception request sec-req-412 created for tenant nordbank-poc-12. Notified security-oncall.

nina-support: Action items: (1) nina-support -> assist customer rotate SCIM token and re-run sync (in 30m). (2) alex-rm -> collect failing SCIM payloads to identify stale group mappings (1h). (3) sam-se -> provide mapping snippet for `auth_method` and confirm allowlist options (ASAP). (4) emma-ps -> follow security exemption (if requested).

alex-rm: Customer will try the claim trim and re-run SSO test tonight. Will update here after they confirm. :pray:
